epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.kind: build-side adaptation input, not upstream code, not a patch
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.consumed_by: tools/build_librime_baseline.ps1 -DUSE_SYSTEM_MARISA:BOOL=ON configure step, injected through CMake's documented CMAKE_PROJECT_opencc_INCLUDE hook (script lines 523, 544-545)
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.why_required: OpenCC 1.1.9 at 556ed224 supports USE_SYSTEM_MARISA=ON at the option level but performs two steps only for its BUNDLED marisa: adding the include directory (deps/opencc/src/CMakeLists.txt:6-8, OFF branch only) and providing a link target for the bare name `marisa` (deps/opencc/src/CMakeLists.txt:118). With an external marisa and no adaptation, OpenCC fails to compile marisa.h.
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.why_upstream_shas_are_not_sufficient: Every SHA in this lock identifies SOURCE content. None of them identifies this file, and none of them cause these two additions to happen. A machine that restored exactly the pinned sources and then configured OpenCC the way the lock describes would NOT reproduce the P1.2 baseline; it would fail with 'marisa.h: No such file or directory'. Reproducing the build therefore requires this file plus -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD:STRING=17 (marisa 0.3.1's public headers use std::string_view and nested namespace definitions, which OpenCC 1.1.9 requests no standard for on MSVC).
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.upstream_alternative_not_taken: A minimal upstream patch (invert the src/CMakeLists.txt:6-8 condition, link ${LIBMARISA} at :118, set CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17 for MSVC) would remove the need for this file. It is described in docs/build/librime-windows-baseline.md section 10.1 and was deliberately NOT applied: third_party/patches/ still does not exist and no upstream byte was changed.

epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.role: The only entry that turns the locked sources into the EpoCanva librime artefacts. Performs no network I/O and installs nothing. Its option set, dependency order and assertions are part of the reproducible recipe; recording the source SHAs without this script would not reproduce the same binaries. Modes: -Mode baseline (default, P1.2 behaviour), -Mode component-probe (P1.4), -Mode english-completion (P2.1). Both component modes reuse -Mode baseline's prefix read-only, refuse to rebuild the four dependencies, and assert that baseline's own rime CMakeCache contains no EPOCANVA_* entry. Each mode's ATTACHED assertion is label-specific, so one mode's configure log cannot certify another mode's build.
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.registered_in_phase: P1.3; re-registered in P1.4 for the two-mode form; in P2.1 for the third mode and the two defect fixes below; in P2.2 and P2.3 because the english-completion mode's expected component-object list grew by english_case.obj and then by english_token.obj; re-registered again in P2.5 because that list grew to eight names (english_space_processor.obj, english_space_policy.obj) and a third DLL needle was added
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.previous_sha256_superseded: 37ec3129949769162480c639d865728dcd6069d8df476e11f0b0dde9e49e1270 (P2.3/P2.4, 1212 lines, six English component objects); before that d6446ee8704a42608528f9bd30f59e0ff61d0b070bbe4455b0a4970fd567f71a (P2.2, 1206 lines, five English objects), 279859fddc053623d218727836375c928a132257bf41d934f749830b036d132e (P2.1, 1203 lines, three modes with four English objects), c3d5297a5f37ff706d0968e3b478e0b118cfb962d28569bef1b87942283fd273 (P1.4, 1051 lines, two modes) and 339c857671fae1f4f4d3eff711d865549f1ca89110c9e0ef784a93f51c3e8566 (P1.3, 828 lines, baseline only)
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.p2_3_object_list_reason: The english-completion mode names every component translation unit it expects to find an object for. When P2.3 added engine/languages/en/english_token.cc the list went from five names to six; leaving it at five would have meant the new layer was never asserted to be in the engine, which is the same class of defect P2.2 recorded in its section 8.2.
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.p2_5_object_list_reason: P2.5 added two more translation units -- engine/languages/en/english_space_policy.cc (the rules) and engine/rime_components/english/english_space_processor.cc (the component that acts on them) -- so the list went from six names to eight and the expected object total from 119 to 121. A third DLL needle, 'epocanva_english_space', was added because that literal is the Processor's registration name: it is live code (english_module.cc passes it to Registry::Register), so its absence in the image means the engine has no space policy at all, and the schema listing it would silently fall back to 'no such processor' (src/rime/engine.cc:310-315 logs and skips).

p2_1_defect_fixes.incremental_mt_false_failure: The old rule 'if no /MT appears in the build log, throw' conflated two different causes: the static CRT not reaching cl (a real failure) and an up-to-date incremental build where MSBuild recompiled nothing and therefore printed no cl command line at all (not a failure - this is exactly the exit 1 that docs/reports/P1.4-component-probe.md section 8 had to record). The two are now separated by a log-independent observation: whether any .obj in the rime tree was written during this run (LastWriteTime >= run start). Objects rewritten but no /MT still throws; nothing rewritten resolves the CRT question from the per-artefact MT_StaticRelease directives that were already read from disk. /MD != 0 still throws unconditionally and every per-artefact ABI assertion is unchanged. Verified: -Mode english-completion without -Fresh and without -Verbose_Build now exits 0, printing 'objects written by this run: 0 of 117'. No forced full rebuild and no fabricated log.
p2_1_defect_fixes.skip_parameter_contract: -Skip 'a,b,c' passed through 'powershell.exe -File' binds as ONE array element, because -File does not split arguments; the old code then matched no name and silently skipped nothing, rebuilding the whole chain (the P1.4 report recorded this accidental behaviour). The value is now re-split on commas, trimmed and lower-cased, and unknown names are refused with '-Skip accepts marisa, yaml-cpp, leveldb, opencc, rime; got: <x>' instead of being ignored. Verified: -Mode baseline -Skip 'marisa,yaml-cpp,leveldb,opencc,rime' exits 0 and prints all five 'skipping' lines.

epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.kind: build-side adaptation input, not upstream code, not a patch
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.consumed_by: tools/build_librime_baseline.ps1 in -Mode component-probe and -Mode english-completion only, in the rime configure step, injected through CMake's documented CMAKE_PROJECT_rime_INCLUDE hook. Never passed in -Mode baseline; since P2.1 the build script itself asserts that baseline's rime CMakeCache holds no EPOCANVA_* and no CMAKE_PROJECT_rime_INCLUDE entry.
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.why_required: Upstream's merged-plugin mechanism has no entry that accepts an out-of-tree source path: third_party/librime/plugins/CMakeLists.txt:29-30 strips every directory prefix off ENV{RIME_PLUGINS} and converts spaces to ';', :33-39 otherwise globs directories out of third_party/librime/plugins/, and sample/CMakeLists.txt:36 states the official instruction as 'link or copy the directory to plugins/'. Creating such a directory would make the pinned checkout dirty, which AGENTS.md section 7 forbids. Generalised in P2.1 to a component LIST (EPOCANVA_RIME_COMPONENT_ROOT + EPOCANVA_RIME_COMPONENT_NAMES + EPOCANVA_RIME_HOOK_LABEL) because the English component needs the language core compiled in beside it; a component that declares no object targets is a FATAL_ERROR rather than a silent omission. This file therefore adds each named EpoCanva component directory as an OBJECT library inside the rime project and attaches its objects to the rime target with target_sources($<TARGET_OBJECTS:...>) via cmake_language(DEFER CALL ...), which CMake documents as running 'as if written at the end of the current directory's CMakeLists.txt file' - i.e. after upstream's add_subdirectory(src) created the target. It is the same generator-expression mechanism upstream itself uses (plugins/CMakeLists.txt:20 feeding src/CMakeLists.txt:35).
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.why_upstream_shas_are_not_sufficient: Without this file a machine holding exactly the pinned sources can only build the engine WITHOUT EpoCanva's components. The component and core sources (engine/rime_components/, engine/languages/en/) are project code, not upstream, and are covered by no SHA in this lock; the DLL identity is recorded per phase report instead (see P1_4_component_probe.artefact_identity and P2_1_english_completion.artefact_identity for why those hashes are per-link identities rather than reproducibility checksums).
epocanva_build_adaptation_inputs.upstream_alternative_not_taken: Putting the component under third_party/librime/plugins/ (official mechanism, but dirties the checkout), or a minimal upstream patch to accept an out-of-tree plugin source directory, or enabling ENABLE_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS (which compiles in plugins_module.cc, a Boost.DLL loader that loads every *.dll in a rime-plugins directory - forbidden by the P1.4 brief). None was applied; third_party/patches/ still does not exist.

verification.fails_loudly: FATAL_ERROR unless PROJECT_NAME is rime, EPOCANVA_RIME_COMPONENT_ROOT is a directory, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS and BUILD_MERGED_PLUGINS are ON, ENABLE_EXTERNAL_PLUGINS is OFF, and EPOCANVA_RIME_COMPONENT_NAMES / EPOCANVA_RIME_HOOK_LABEL are set; every named component must have a CMakeLists.txt and must export non-empty epocanva_rime_<name>_object_targets naming targets that still exist at attach time. artefact_identity.note: The import library is byte-identical between the two modes and dumpbin reports 571 export names in both images, so compiling the component in added no exported symbol and no new ABI surface. The DLLs differ, and each contains the component's strings only in the component build.
artefact_identity.dll_hash_is_not_a_reproducibility_checks: Two builds of the same sources produced different component DLL hashes (the two values above). cmp -l shows the files differ by 28 bytes only, at the PE TimeDateStamp, two debug-directory timestamps and a 16-byte PDB GUID; file size (2670080 bytes), rime.lib and the 571-name export table are unchanged. So the recorded value identifies THE BINARY THAT PRODUCED A GIVEN RESULT and proves baseline != component; it must not be used as a 'same hash means same build' gate. The time-independent judgements are: 113 -> 115 object files, component strings present in the component DLL and absent from the baseline, empty export-set difference, and the runtime diagnostic counters. P2_2_english_case_preservation.what_p2_2_adds: ASCII case mapping with original-text preservation. The completer classifies the raw input, lowers it only into a separate lookup key, and re-applies the input's case shape to the canonical dictionary word to build the display/commit text. Single-letter uppercase input is treated as initial-capital (H -> Hello). Mixed-case input (HeL, hEL, iPh) is not completed: it yields the original candidate only, and is counted as a case decision, never as a lexicon load failure. Raw input is never modified in place; the default commit remains exactly what the user typed.
P2_2_english_case_preservation.the_four_texts_are_distinct: raw input (never mutated, returned by context->preedit()) / lookup key (lowercase ASCII, derived, not stored) / canonical dictionary word (the lexicon's own lowercase text) / display-and-commit candidate (canonical re-cased). english_case.h documents this separation at the API comment level, and the core test suite compares a byte-for-byte copy of every input buffer after every call.
P2_2_english_case_preservation.not_unicode_case_folding: Only the 26 ASCII letter pairs are mapped, by explicit byte-range comparison (no <cctype>, no towlower/towlower, no std::locale, no setlocale). Non-ASCII byte sequences are classified kNotAlphabetic and refused; the docs and the enum name say 'ASCII case style', and no document calls this Unicode case folding or general case mapping.

P2_3_english_token_protection.what_p2_3_adds: A limited English word-form layer with protected-text fidelity. engine/languages/en/english_token.{h,cc} answers, as named values rather than a bool, whether the input is a complete entry, a queryable prefix, which byte class stopped it and where; english_case.{h,cc} treats the two ASCII word delimiters as case-transparent so don't maps to Don't and DON'T while Co-Operate stays mixed and is refused; english_lexicon.{h,cc} validates entries through the same grammar the query layer uses and reports a misplaced delimiter as the new status illegal-word-form, distinct from illegal-word which means a byte the word alphabet never had; prefix_completer.cc replaced P2.1's key + '{' range bound with the prefix successor.
P2_3_english_token_protection.range_bound_change: P2.1 bounded the matched range at key + '{', which is only correct while every byte that can FOLLOW the prefix is below 0x7B. That held for an a-z-only word list and stops being a property of the algorithm the moment entries contain U+0027 and U+002D. The bound is now succ(key) = key with its last byte incremented, whose correctness proof mentions neither 'z' nor the entry alphabet. tests/english_core/main.cc case 23 asserts both edges as index pairs derived by hand from a ten-row table (co- -> [1,2) finds co-operate and must NOT find coopt; don' -> [6,7) finds don't and must NOT find done), plus a loop that re-checks every entry inside the range for the prefix and both neighbours for its absence.
P2_3_english_token_protection.protection_mechanism: The fixture schema's speller/alphabet now contains, besides the 52 ASCII letters, the two word delimiters, the ten digits and the marks @ . _ : / \ ? & = # % +. This is not a relaxation of the rule; it is how the rule can exist at all. A byte outside speller/alphabet is dropped by Speller::ProcessKeyEvent (src/rime/gear/speller.cc:109-110) so the composition would stop before it and the translator would never learn the token was technical; worse, src/rime/gear/fallback_segmentor.cc:16-56 would then append one-byte raw segments for the leftovers and this translator would be queried about the LETTER part alone, completing 'user' while the user typed an address. With the marks in the alphabet, AbcSegmentor::Proceed (src/rime/gear/abc_segmentor.cc:39-57, membership test at :46) keeps the whole token inside ONE abc segment and the language core refuses it as a unit. No new Processor or Segmentor was needed, and kDefaultModules and the upstream source are untouched.
P2_3_english_token_protection.segment_scope_evidence: queries_covering_whole_input and queries_covering_part_of_input are event counts (english_diagnostics.h), so no composition text or offset crosses the C boundary. Across the whole token-protection run: queries=405, whole=405, part=0. Every query this process made was about the entire composition, which is what proves no partial completion was offered and discarded.
